data2 <- read.csv(paste0(base_dir, "data/outputs/aim2_onlygen3/experiment_2.csv"))

# Data manipulation

```{r}
data <- data %>% select(-q_value_pop2) # remove, and then decide if we need to 1-pop or now 

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    hybrid_status = case_when(
      str_detect(ind_id, "IND") ~ str_split_i(ind_id, "_", 2),
      str_detect(ind_id, "F1") ~ "F1",
      str_detect(ind_id, "F2") ~ "F2",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B2POP1") ~ "B2POP1",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B2POP2") ~ "B2POP2",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B3POP1") ~ "B3POP1",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B3POP2") ~ "B3POP2"
    )
  )

# JC_orientation means pop1 == JC? -- doesn't necessary align with the BC2POP1 labels
data <- data %>%
  group_by(experiment_ID, bootstrap_ID, run_id) %>%
  mutate(
    JC_orientation = mean(
      q_value_pop1[hybrid_status == "JC"],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) > 0.5,
    
    JC = if_else(
      JC_orientation,
      q_value_pop1,
      1 - q_value_pop1
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Correct labels 
data <- data %>% mutate(
    hybrid_status = case_when(
      # Known pure individuals
      str_detect(ind_id, "_JC$") ~ "JC",
      str_detect(ind_id, "_JA$") ~ "JA",
      
      # F1 / F2
      str_detect(ind_id, "F1") ~ "F1",
      str_detect(ind_id, "F2") ~ "F2",
      
      # B2
      # JC_orientation = True, means that pop2=JC, pop1=JA
      str_detect(ind_id, "B2POP1") & JC_orientation ~ "B2_JA",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B2POP2") & JC_orientation ~ "B2_JC",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B2POP1") & !JC_orientation ~ "B2_JA",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B2POP2") & !JC_orientation ~ "B2_JC",
      
      # B3
      str_detect(ind_id, "B3POP1") & JC_orientation ~ "B3_JA",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B3POP2") & JC_orientation ~ "B3_JC",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B3POP1") & !JC_orientation ~ "B3_JA",
      str_detect(ind_id, "B3POP2") & !JC_orientation ~ "B3_JC",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
) %>% select(-q_value_pop1, -JC_orientation)
```

# Overall_Accuracy vs. threshold 
```{r}
# B3_JC
B3_JCs <- data %>% filter(hybrid_status %in% c("B3_JC"))

# Threshold from 0.85..0.99 
thresholds <- seq(0.85, 0.99, by = 0.01)

# Compute confusion matrix counts for each threshold
confusion_matrices <- crossing(B3_JCs, threshold = thresholds) %>%
  mutate(
    # Classification rule: >= threshold is called "pure", < threshold is called "hybrid"
    predicted_class = if_else(JC >= threshold, "pure", "hybrid"),
    
    # Standardize true label (treating B3_JC / BC3_JC as the true "hybrid" class)
    true_class = if_else(str_detect(hybrid_status, "B3_JC"), "hybrid", "pure")
  ) %>%
  group_by(threshold) %>%
  summarize(
    # True Positives: True hybrid correctly predicted as hybrid
    TP = sum(predicted_class == "hybrid" & true_class == "hybrid"),
    # False Negatives: True hybrid incorrectly predicted as pure (mislabeled)
    FN = sum(predicted_class == "pure" & true_class == "hybrid"),
    # False Positives: True pure incorrectly predicted as hybrid
    FP = sum(predicted_class == "hybrid" & true_class == "pure"),
    # True Negatives: True pure correctly predicted as pure
    TN = sum(predicted_class == "pure" & true_class == "pure"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Overall_Accuracy = (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN),
    Accuracy = TP / (TP + FP),
    Efficiency = TP / (TP + FN)
  )

# View the resulting summary table of confusion matrices per threshold
print(confusion_matrices)

ggplot(confusion_matrices, aes(x = threshold, y = Overall_Accuracy)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "darkblue", size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent_format(Overall_Accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0.85, 0.99, by = 0.02)) +
  labs(
    title = "BC3_JC only",
    # subtitle = "Evaluating classification performance across thresholds 0.85 to 0.99",
    x = "Identification Threshold",
    y = "Overall_Accuracy"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

```

# Basic BC2 and BC3, Accuracy

```{r}
BC_JCs <- data %>% filter(hybrid_status %in% c("B2_JC", "B3_JC"))

# 1. Define the sequence of thresholds from 0.85 to 0.99 by 0.01
bottom_threshold <- 0.70
top_threshold <- 0.99
thresholds <- seq(bottom_threshold, top_threshold, by = 0.01)

# 2. Get all unique hybrid classes present in your dataset
hybrid_classes <- unique(BC_JCs$hybrid_status)

# 3. Create a grid combining data, thresholds, and target hybrid classes
# This allows us to evaluate performance for each hybrid type independently (One-vs-All)
multi_class_matrices <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    BC_JCs, 
    threshold = thresholds,
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Classification rule: >= threshold is called "pure", < threshold is called the target hybrid
    predicted_class = if_else(JC >= threshold, "pure", "hybrid"),
    
    # Check if the row's true hybrid status matches the current target class being evaluated
    true_class = if_else(hybrid_status == "JC", "pure", "hybrid")
  ) %>% group_by(hybrid_status, threshold) %>%
  summarize(
    TP = sum(predicted_class == "hybrid" & true_class == "hybrid"),
    FN = sum(predicted_class == "pure" & true_class == "hybrid"),
    FP = sum(predicted_class == "hybrid" & true_class == "pure"),
    TN = sum(predicted_class == "pure" & true_class == "pure"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Overall_Accuracy = (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN),
    Accuracy = if_else((TP + FP) > 0, TP / (TP + FP), 0),
    Efficiency = if_else((TP + FN) > 0, TP / (TP + FN), 0)
  )

# View the result summary table
print(multi_class_matrices)

# 4. Plot Threshold vs Overall_Accuracy, faceted by each hybrid class
accuracy_plot <- ggplot(multi_class_matrices, aes(x = threshold, y = Accuracy, color = hybrid_status, linetype = hybrid_status)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(Overall_Accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(bottom_threshold, top_threshold, by = 0.02)) +
  labs(
    #itle = "Identification Threshold vs. Overall_Accuracy by Hybrid Class",
    # subtitle = "Comparing performance curves across all hybrid populations on a single plot",
    x = "Identification Threshold",
    y = "Accuracy",
    color = "Hybrid Class",
    linetype = "Hybrid Class"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
accuracy_plot

efficiency_plot <- ggplot(multi_class_matrices, aes(x = threshold, y = Efficiency, color = hybrid_status, linetype = hybrid_status)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(Overall_Accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(bottom_threshold, top_threshold, by = 0.02)) +
  labs(
    #itle = "Identification Threshold vs. Overall_Accuracy by Hybrid Class",
    # subtitle = "Comparing performance curves across all hybrid populations on a single plot",
    x = "Identification Threshold",
    y = "Efficiency",
    color = "Hybrid Class",
    linetype = "Hybrid Class"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
efficiency_plot

preformance_plot <- ggplot(multi_class_matrices, aes(x = threshold, y = (Accuracy * Efficiency), color = hybrid_status, linetype = hybrid_status)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(Overall_Accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(bottom_threshold, top_threshold, by = 0.02)) +
  labs(
    #itle = "Identification Threshold vs. Overall_Accuracy by Hybrid Class",
    # subtitle = "Comparing performance curves across all hybrid populations on a single plot",
    x = "Identification Threshold",
    y = "Preformance",
    color = "Hybrid Class",
    linetype = "Hybrid Class"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

accuracy_plot

accuracy_plot + efficiency_plot + 
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") & 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Truncated to show curve of both 
```{r}
# Include the pure parental class 'JC' so true positives/negatives can be calculated
BC_JCs <- data %>% filter(hybrid_status %in% c("B2_JC", "B3_JC", "JC"))

bottom_threshold <- 0.75
top_threshold <- 0.99
thresholds <- seq(bottom_threshold, top_threshold, by = 0.01)

multi_class_matrices <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    BC_JCs, 
    threshold = thresholds
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Rule: values strictly greater than or equal to threshold are classified as pure parent
    predicted_class = if_else(JC >= threshold, "pure", "hybrid"),
    
    # Ground truth assignment
    true_class = if_else(hybrid_status == "JC", "pure", "hybrid")
  ) %>% 
  # We group by hybrid_status so we can see how Overall_Accuracy changes for B2_JC and B3_JC independently
  group_by(hybrid_status, threshold) %>%
  summarize(
    TP = sum(predicted_class == "hybrid" & true_class == "hybrid"),
    FN = sum(predicted_class == "pure" & true_class == "hybrid"),
    FP = sum(predicted_class == "hybrid" & true_class == "pure"),
    TN = sum(predicted_class == "pure" & true_class == "pure"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Overall_Accuracy = (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN),
    Accuracy = if_else((TP + FP) > 0, TP / (TP + FP), 0),
    Efficiency = if_else((TP + FN) > 0, TP / (TP + FN), 0)
  ) %>%
  # Filter out the pure JC rows from the final plotting data so you only plot curves for your hybrids
  filter(hybrid_status %in% c("B2_JC", "B3_JC"))

# 2. Build the tailored plot for B2_JC (0.75 - 0.85)
plot_b2 <- ggplot(
    data = filter(multi_class_matrices, hybrid_status == "B2_JC"), 
    aes(x = threshold, y = Overall_Accuracy)
  ) +
  geom_line(color = "#F8766D", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(color = "#F8766D", size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(Overall_Accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0.75, 0.85, by = 0.02)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.75, 0.85), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Identification Threshold (B2_JC)", y = "Overall_Accuracy") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# 3. Build the tailored plot for B3_JC (0.85 - 0.90)
plot_b3 <- ggplot(
    data = filter(multi_class_matrices, hybrid_status == "B3_JC"), 
    aes(x = threshold, y = Overall_Accuracy)
  ) +
  geom_line(color = "#00BFC4", linewidth = 1.1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(color = "#00BFC4", size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(Overall_Accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0.85, 0.90, by = 0.01)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.85, 0.90), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Identification Threshold (B3_JC)", y = "") + # Remove y-axis label to avoid repetition
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(), # Hide y text if aligned next to plot_b2
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )

# 4. Stitch them together side by side
plot_b2 + plot_b3


```
